patterns: Writing about writing wins big: James Clear's 'Writing is the superpower of humankind' did ~96k views and 967 saves. Saves outran likes by a lot, so people keep it to reread.
The empty first page is a shared feeling: the notebook-you-save-for-a-better-self line and a three-pages-of-nonsense ink test both point at permission to write badly.
Used bookstores run on characters and finds: a named owner (Gabor), a 2003 birthday note tucked inside a book, and a door-holding story all drew replies on modest accounts.
Handwriting as a constraint: a journalist limited to pen and paper in court filled 10 pages in a day, and people answered the handwriting compliment more than the trial.
Low-capacity framing beats routines for ADHD posts: 'my ADHD brain would rather do a ritual than a wellness routine' lands better than advice lists.
Skip: Yongfook's DocuSign joke and Vassallo's F1 and Mbappe posts are big but off-brand. 'Magazine cover' and 'editorial design' searches are mostly AI prompts and fandom noise.

reply_ideas.description: a short post about buying a notebook to organize your life, then saving it for a future self whose handwriting deserves the first page
reply_ideas.reply_text: That first page has more pressure on it than any other page in the book. Some people scribble on it on purpose just to get past it. Do you think it's really the handwriting we're waiting on, or a tidier version of our life that feels worth writing down?

reply_ideas.description: a travel podcaster found a great used bookstore run by a fellow named Gabor and admits he may have bought books
reply_ideas.reply_text: Gabor sounds like the kind of owner who knows where every book is, even when the shelves say otherwise. What did you end up carrying out? I'm more curious about the one you didn't plan on than the ones you went in for.

reply_ideas.description: a journalist covering a Texas trial where only pen and paper are allowed in the courtroom; he filled 10 pages yesterday and keeps getting compliments on his handwriting
reply_ideas.reply_text: Ten pages by hand in one day of testimony is serious work. Have you built up your own shorthand by now, or are you writing it all out and hoping you can still read it tonight? I'd love to know how you mark the lines you already know you'll want to quote.

video_tip: 15 seconds, no face. Overhead on textured cream paper, a hand opens a brand-new notebook, pauses over the first page, then writes a plain grocery list on it and turns to page two. Pen and paper sounds only, no music. End on a card that reads 'What's on your first page?' Pairs with the first-page post.

x_posts.title: The first page
x_posts.text:
Is anyone else sitting on a notebook they bought months ago and still haven't written in, because the first page feels like it has to be good?

I've started to think the first page should be allowed to be a grocery list.
